text:
Maya: Heads up — after the int4v2 quant bring-up for mag-17b we see reproducible divergence once the prompt crosses ~16k tokens. Running the new "sherlock" anchor-scan harness now :eyes:
Zach: Can you paste the exact run command + the minimal repro prompt?
Maya: sure:
```
sherlock run --model mag-17b-int4v2 --harness anchor-scan --prefix bigdoc.txt --max-tokens 32000 --snapshot-every 1024 --out /tmp/sherlock/run1
```
The short repro is the legal-doc style prefix in bigdoc.txt (I can DM the file).
Tara: Is the divergence present on float32 baseline too or only quantized?
Maya: baseline float32 matches gold all the way to 32k. Quant path diverges starting ~token 16412. Quick metrics from the harness: logp_mse=8.2e-4, token_shift_count=2 at token 16412 (expected 'companion' -> got 'company').
Sam: Did you try toggling rotary rescale / posscale?
Maya: Yes. rot_rescale=false reduces amplitude of the drift (max_kl 0.0031 -> 0.0018) but doesn't eliminate it. That suggests a KV anchoring or prefill stride interaction rather than pure RoPE math.
Li: Can we get a targeted KV dump around the boundary (layers 18-24 + top-kv pages)? kv-bot can schedule.
kv-bot: Scheduled KV snapshot job id=kvdump-20260405-0915, artifacts: s3://redwood-qa/kvdumps/kvdump-20260405-0915.tar.gz :robot_face:
Zach: Thanks. Also try disabling the 'pack' stage in quant pipeline (pack = true -> false) — we saw pack-related reorderiness in other models.
Tara: I ran a quick matrix earlier: int8-pack=false -> no drift; int4-pack=true -> drift. So pack+int4 looks suspicious.
Maya: Good detail. Plan I'm executing tonight: 1) run sherlock bisect focusing on quant stages (quantize -> prune -> pack) across int4 variants 2) capture per-layer KV snapshots at the anchor window +/- 2048 tokens 3) run n=50 stability sweep and produce token divergence histogram + earliest-diff index
Sam: +1. If bisect points to pack, we can try reverting the pack micro-optim and re-evaluate throughput impact.
Zach: If you get a candidate commit, ping me. I'll prioritize a local reproducer and a short-run with pack disabled on Dedicated to verify.
Maya: uploading initial diff and small trace (attached to the kvdump). link: https://s3.redwood-qa/kvdumps/kvdump-20260405-0915/trace-summary.txt
Tara: One more thought — check prefix eviction threshold config. If pack changes shard layout, eviction heuristics might evict/shift prefill fragments across the boundary. That could create deterministic token shifts.
Maya: Good call. I'll add eviction threshold toggles to the bisect matrix.
Li: I'll also run a microbench that compares raw KV keys/positions between float32 vs int4-packed at the boundary and dump a key diff report.
Maya: sweet. I'll post morning results. cc @Zach @Tara. Thanks all :thumbsup:
